decisive_items: complete atrioventricular block with inferior ST-segment elevation
uncle and two sisters had sudden cardiac death at a young age
response.rationale: Severe lactic acidosis, hyperglycemia, transaminitis, brainstem signs, and cardiac conduction block with maternal-pattern sudden death point to a mitochondrial/metabolic cytopathy; negative WES is consistent because mitochondrial DNA is not covered. R6 captures the arrhythmia but not the multisystem metabolic picture.

rejected.why: Explains coma/brainstem signs but not lactic acidosis, AV block, or family sudden death.
Family sudden death is a risk pattern, not a diagnosis; ignores metabolic acidosis and AV block.
BP 145/50 is not a hypertensive emergency; normal coronaries and troponin argue against it.
CPVT typically causes exercise-induced polymorphic VT, not AV block, and does not explain lactic acidosis.
No LV hypertrophy or typical HCM features; LVEF 59% and metabolic findings unexplained.
No right precordial Brugada ECG pattern; inferior ST elevation and AV block are not characteristic.
Autonomic dysfunction does not explain AV block, family sudden death, or severe lactic acidosis.
Hypertension is background only; BP is not severely elevated and does not explain coma/AV block/lactate.
No QT prolongation described; complete AV block and metabolic acidosis are not LQTS features.
Captures arrhythmia/syncope/family history but misses the decisive metabolic and multisystem findings.
No ARVC imaging/ECG criteria; normal LVEF and metabolic acidosis unexplained.
